title: OSV severity arrays cause vulnerable dependencies to disappear
trigger: Scan a dependency whose OSV vulnerability contains a standard severity array, including an empty array alongside database_specific.severity.
impact: _mapSeverity calls toUpperCase on an array. The enclosing catch swallows the TypeError, returning and caching zero or partial findings; policy can pass for a vulnerable dependency.
evidence: repro.cjs B01: synthetic OSV CVSS array yields zero findings, otherwise identical string-severity control yields HIGH. OSSF schema https://ossf.github.io/osv-schema/ defines severity as an array of objects.
fix: Parse OSV severity objects/CVSS vectors and database_specific fallback without discarding the vulnerability when severity is unknown.

title: Unavailable dependency scans become cached policy passes
trigger: Dependency lookup fetch rejects or returns a non-OK response.
impact: The scanner returns an empty list and caches it for one hour. runDependencyScan reports zero vulnerabilities and policyPassed=true, so an unavailable scan is indistinguishable from a clean result.
evidence: repro.cjs B02: stub fetch throws; manager returns total=0 and policyPassed=true; repeated package lookup makes no second fetch call. Clean package and positive vulnerability controls run in B01.
fix: Represent unavailable/error separately, avoid caching failed lookups as clean data, and prevent policy success when required scan coverage is incomplete.

title: Infrastructure scanner stubs violate the manager result contract
trigger: Run docker_container, docker_image or k8s_yaml pipeline security node.
impact: Stub scanners return a result object. runInfrastructureScan assigns it to vulnerabilities and calls .forEach, throwing before producing a scan result. The advertised infrastructure nodes cannot execute scans.
evidence: repro.cjs B03: all three manager calls reject with forEach error. Registering an array-returning scanner control succeeds. Pipeline caller confirmed at pipeline-manager.js940-954; no Electron delegation is used on this path.
fix: Wire the intended backend scanners and normalize their return values to the manager contract; until available, return an explicit unsupported/error result rather than success-shaped stubs.

title: Policy early returns ignore configured vulnerability maxima
trigger: Set Fail on Critical only while configuring a maximum for High, Medium or Low, then exceed that maximum with no Critical findings.
impact: The critical-only branch returns before checking the lower-severity maxima. Similar earlier returns skip other configured maxima, allowing scans above the displayed limits to pass.
evidence: repro.cjs B04: maxima=1 and counts=200 for high/medium/low still pass; one critical fails as the positive control.
fix: Evaluate every configured numeric maximum before applying the failOn severity rule; document how the two policy controls combine.

title: Asynchronous JavaScript unit tests report PASS before completion
trigger: Test Code returns a Promise that performs assertions asynchronously.
impact: testFunc return value is ignored. The engine reports PASS with zero failed assertions and runs teardown before the Promise settles; later failures cannot update that returned result.
evidence: repro.cjs B10 queues a deterministic failing assertion with a timer stub, observes PASS first, then runs the queued callback and confirms the failure. No real side effects or unhandled rejection are used.
fix: Await setup/test/teardown results in an async-capable runner and define a timeout/cancellation contract.

title: Python framework tests are defined but never discovered or run
trigger: Choose pytest and supply a normal def test_failure(): assert False test, or define unittest.TestCase tests without a manual runner.
impact: The engine executes source as a script and marks it PASS if definition succeeds. It never invokes pytest/unittest discovery, so a failing framework test can pass without executing any assertion.
evidence: repro.cjs B12 captures the exact generated Python program, runs it in the bundled local Python, and verifies exit0/PASS while test_failure remains only a callable definition. Pyodide execution is stubbed; framework discovery absence is source-proven.
fix: Invoke the selected framework and derive status/counts from its actual results, or expose only an explicitly documented script-assertion mode.

title: Live runner advanced checks inspect the creator preview instead
trigger: Run a saved visual web test containing screenshot baseline/comparison, performance or accessibility steps.
impact: Normal steps use the supplied runner iframeWin, but every advanced step hardcodes vwt-iframe, the creator preview. It captures/checks an unrelated or blank page and can report false passes/failures, especially during concurrent runs.
evidence: repro.cjs B13 invokes all four actions with a distinct runner window; all receive vwt-iframe. Other affected calls at143/166; live-runner creates its own unnamed iframe at836-841 and passes its window at1006/1022.
fix: Accept the actual runner window/iframe element in AdvancedAssertions and pass it from each execution context; avoid a global creator DOM id.

title: Visual builders generate Robot code without required cell separators
trigger: Create a Click Element step and generate Browser-Only or Universal Robot code, then run it as Robot Framework.
impact: Library BrowserLibrary/SeleniumLibrary uses one space instead of a Robot cell separator; templates similarly emit Click Element #submit with one-space argument separation. Robot does not parse the import/arguments as intended, so no-code generated suites cannot run correctly. VWT-generated Robot and Monaco snippets share this issue.
evidence: repro.cjs B21 captures actual generated code and contrasts its one-cell rows with correctly delimited controls. Official Robot Framework User Guide space-separated format requires two or more spaces or a tab between tokens: https://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/RobotFrameworkUserGuide.html#space-separated-format . Actual Robot runner was not installed/executed. Related generation at nocode-builder.js19 and visual-web-tester.js765-767.
fix: Generate properly separated Robot cells and indentation throughout imports/templates/snippets; encode multiline arguments with Robot continuation syntax and verify generated suites using Robot dry-run.

title: Playwright desktop runner depends on external Node and launch-directory dependencies
trigger: Start installed desktop app on a machine without PATH Node, or from a directory outside the source project that has no matching node_modules/playwright.
impact: Playwright tests fail before opening a browser; runner writes into process.cwd/.temp_exec and invokes external node instead of a packaged runtime. package.json declares Playwright only as devDependency.
evidence: driver-repro.cjs executes the unchanged runner with inert fs/process stubs, proves launch-CWD path and bare node command; missing-node fixture returns failure. Source package.json establishes only devDependency. Full installer runtime not tested.
fix: Package a supported execution runtime/dependencies and browser payload; resolve a writable per-user execution directory and explicit runtime/package paths rather than launch cwd or PATH.

title: Graph pipelines report failing nodes as SUCCESS and continue execution
trigger: Run any graph node whose production runner returns FAILURE (or the Playwright IPC returns ERROR).
impact: overallStatus remains SUCCESS and downstream nodes execute even when onFailure is stop; failed tests, clones and security scans can produce a green pipeline.
evidence: repro.cjs EXE-01 executes unchanged GraphEngine: SUCCESS runs both nodes; FAILED correctly stops; actual FAILURE and ERROR both return SUCCESS, with FAILURE executing the dependent node. Production pipeline-manager.js returns FAILURE throughout.
fix: Normalize the shared result enum and treat FAILURE/ERROR as failing outcomes before executing dependents; test the production runner contract.

title: Security nodes created by the visual editor never reach the graph security handlers
trigger: Drag Security Scan or Security Gate from the visual editor palette and run the graph.
impact: Editor nodes use security-scan/security-gate; dispatcher expects security_scan/security_gate. Both fall through to runTestSuite(undefined), so no scan or gate runs. EXE-01 additionally masks the failure as pipeline success.
evidence: EXE-02 creates both nodes through original VisualEditor._handleDrop and runs original runGraphPipeline: zero scans and two suite calls with undefined. Control security_scan node invokes the scanner once.
fix: Use one canonical node-type enum shared by the palette, editor, configuration and graph executor.

title: Security gate cannot receive the preceding scan's results
trigger: Run connected security_scan -> security_gate nodes, including an imported underscore-type graph or after correcting EXE-02, with scan findings exceeding the gate threshold.
impact: Scanner returns securityResults as an ordinary result field, but GraphEngine transfers only result.artifacts. Neither inputs.securityResults nor context.lastSecurityResults is populated. The gate treats missing data as SUCCESS and skips thresholds.
evidence: EXE-03 feeds a scan with one critical issue and a zero-critical gate: original handlers print No security scan results to check. Control job providing artifacts.securityResults causes the same gate to print FAILED. This defect is independent of the type mismatch and status mismatch.
fix: Publish scan results through the agreed artifact contract or explicitly resolve parent results; fail or report an indeterminate gate when required scan evidence is missing.

title: Website test result contract makes every successful website test fail
trigger: Execute a website suite through executeSuiteCore, including ordinary URL suites and pipeline website suites.
impact: executeWebsiteIntegration returns status, output and error but no success flag, while executeSuiteCore checks result.success. Passing Robot results and the successful no-code path become FAILURE.
evidence: EXE-04 runs the original website integration with a stub successful Robot execution and fake iframe load; direct status is SUCCESS and success is undefined, then executeSuiteCore returns FAILURE. A success:true contract control returns SUCCESS.
fix: Standardize execution adapters on the same result contract, translating the website adapter status explicitly if necessary.

title: Successful test summaries containing '0 failed' are reclassified as failures
trigger: A successful runner emits a normal summary such as '10 passed, 0 failed', or logs an expected exception/negative test name.
impact: Substring matching overrides authoritative SUCCESS with FAILURE; standard test summaries and benign diagnostics break single runs, linear pipelines and graph suite artifacts.
evidence: EXE-06 invokes original runTestSuite with identical successful adapter results: '10 passed' succeeds, '10 passed, 0 failed' and 'Expected exception handled' fail. An adapter FAILURE control stays FAILURE.
fix: Use structured runner status/exit codes and assertions for pass/fail; leave stdout as diagnostic text.

title: Pipeline execution silently skips configured data-driven rows
trigger: Add a suite with a dataSetId to either linear or graph pipeline; both invoke runTestSuite with silent=true.
impact: The !silent condition suppresses the dataset loop rather than just its UI. Only one unexpanded template runs, so parameterized cases are skipped and pipeline coverage differs from manually running the same suite.
evidence: EXE-07 invokes original runTestSuite twice with a two-row dataset. Manual run selects runDataDrivenTest; silent run bypasses it and calls executeSuiteCore once. pipeline-manager.js lines 460 and 1061 supply silent=true.
fix: Separate UI visibility from execution semantics; always execute configured dataset rows, accepting silent and graph inputs independently.

title: Concurrent local-storage mutations overwrite each other
trigger: Delete a view containing at least two suites, use bulk tag operations, or let ensureDemoSuites enqueue multiple saveSuite calls.
impact: Each async mutation snapshots the entire array before awaiting, then writes its stale copy. deleteView unassigns only one of two suites; initial demo inserts and simultaneous changes can silently disappear.
evidence: EXE-09 first verifies sequential updates preserve two changes, then concurrent original updateSuite calls preserve only one. It also invokes original deleteView's async forEach with two suites and proves only one loses view_id. The same read/await/write pattern exists in saveSuite/deleteSuite.
fix: Serialize local read-modify-write transactions, or make the local mutation atomic without an await gap; await caller batches and provide completion/error handling.

title: Migrating version history disconnects it from the active version-control UI
trigger: Accept the startup IndexedDB migration after saving suite_versions_* history.
impact: All migrated history disappears from history, restore and export because the original localStorage keys are deleted while the active VersionControl still reads those keys. Later updates start a separate localStorage history rather than extending the migrated history. The IndexedDB records remain recoverable programmatically.
evidence: repro.cjs S01 saves one active VersionControl snapshot, migrates through a memory-only adapter, verifies copied history exists and active history becomes empty. version-control.js:39-41,82,110 still use localStorage/window.versionControl; script.js:775-780,2095-2099 save to it. indexeddb-version-storage.js:347 initializes only window.indexedDBVersionControl; no source caller connects it to window.versionControl.
fix: Make the application and UI use one consistent async version-control interface before migrating. Keep the original keys until migrated history has been verified through the active reader and restore/export operations.

title: Collaboration imports and snapshot restores report success without persisting
trigger: Import a single-suite JSON file, import a backend share, or restore a snapshot from the collaboration modal.
impact: These operations mutate window.testSuites only. They neither save through the configured backend nor refresh the real suite list, yet show success. A subsequent storage refresh or restart discards the imported/restored changes.
evidence: repro.cjs S04 exercises all three paths with fake currentStorage save/update spies: arrays change and success messages appear, but save/update counts remain zero. Equivalent bad calls: collaboration-ui2.js:142-144,465-473. A whole-source scan finds no definition of saveTestSuites or renderSuites. Actual APIs are currentStorage.saveSuite/updateSuite and renderTestSuites (script.js:751-787,1496).
fix: Await currentStorage.saveSuite for imports and updateSuite for restoration, then refresh through the storage subscription/renderTestSuites. Show success only after persistence succeeds, and surface failures without mutating the authoritative collection prematurely.

title: Generated CI pipelines can succeed when executed tests fail
trigger: Use the generated workflow with an HTTP 200 execution response containing mixed passes/failures, or zero passes with ordinary JSON whitespace.
impact: GitHub Actions rejects only the exact substring "passed":0, so mixed failures and whitespace-formatted all-fail responses produce success. Generated GitLab (lines 283-288) and Jenkins (335-339) gate only on HTTP status and ignore test outcomes entirely. Their green result can misrepresent failed automated tests.
evidence: repro.cjs S13 captures generated templates and checks their exact condition against compact all-fail, mixed-failure and whitespace-formatted fixtures. Compact all-fail is rejected; the other two pass the GitHub condition. Source confirms GitLab/Jenkins never inspect body outcomes. This is template/static proof; no CI platform, backend, shell command or real pipeline was executed. A production backend contract is not present in this repository, so the finding is conditional on its returning execution summaries in HTTP 200 as implied by the generator's own passed check.
fix: Specify the execution response contract, parse JSON structurally and fail on any failed/error result or missing required summary. If execution is asynchronous, poll its final result before reporting success. Apply the same contract to all three generators.

title: Saving a zero vulnerability limit silently restores defaults
trigger: Enter 0 for maximum High, Medium or Low and save the security policy.
impact: parseInt(value)||default treats an intentional zero as absent, storing 5,20 or50. Users cannot require zero issues through these fields.
evidence: repro.cjs B05 saves all fields as zero: maxCritical remains0 while the other maxima become5/20/50.
fix: Use explicit integer validation and default only for missing or invalid values, preserving zero.

title: Security Center suite actions reference an unimplemented storage API
trigger: Run a manual scan and click Save as Suite, or select Scan Selected Suite.
impact: Save always reports Test storage not available. Selected-suite scan always reports no selection because neither window.testStorage nor window._currentSuiteId is assigned by this repository; the application actually uses currentStorage/testSuites/editingSuiteId.
evidence: repro.cjs B06 prepares results and invokes save: no persistence call, unavailable error. Repository-wide assignment search finds no testStorage definition; current-suite guards are at security-ui.js137-163.
fix: Use the application's actual storage and suite-selection state, await its API as required, and refresh the real suite list.

title: Critical vulnerabilities sort after Low in scan results
trigger: Display a scan with mixed severities.
impact: CRITICAL maps to0, then ||4 changes it to4. The most severe findings are placed last instead of first.
evidence: repro.cjs B07 renders four unique severity markers and confirms LOW precedes CRITICAL.
fix: Use nullish fallback or an explicit undefined check so severity rank zero remains zero.

title: Saving scan history permanently drops records beyond51
trigger: Save more than51 security scans.
impact: _saveToHistory calls getHistory() with its default limit50 before adding the newest record. Despite MAX_HISTORY=100, older entries are irreversibly removed on every write and dashboard history cannot reach100.
evidence: repro.cjs B08 saves80 unique records and getHistory(100) contains51.
fix: Read the full retained history when appending, then apply MAX_HISTORY once; keep retrieval limits separate from persistence.

title: JavaScript unit setup variables are out of scope in the test
trigger: Define const fixture=42 in Setup Code and assert(fixture===42) in Test Code.
impact: Setup and test are different Function instances. Ordinary local fixture declarations disappear before the test, which fails with ReferenceError despite successful setup.
evidence: repro.cjs B09: setup fixture case returns FAIL/fixture is not defined; inline assert(true) control passes.
fix: Execute setup/test in a shared lexical scope or expose a documented explicit fixture context shared with teardown.

title: Unit test failures skip teardown
trigger: An assertion or test statement throws before configured Teardown Code.
impact: Execution jumps to the outer catch, skipping cleanup. Resources/state created by setup remain and can contaminate later tests. The generated Python block has the same placement problem at912-932.
evidence: repro.cjs B11: failing assert leaves cleanup counter0; passing control increments it to1.
fix: Run teardown in a finally block for both JavaScript and Python, preserve the primary failure, and report cleanup failures separately.

title: Accessibility check passes completely unlabelled controls without IDs
trigger: Check a page containing input, select or textarea with no id and no label/ARIA accessible name.
impact: The if(id) guard skips the entire label check for these controls and can return passed=true, providing false accessibility assurance.
evidence: repro.cjs B14: bare unlabelled input passes; otherwise equivalent id=username input fails.
fix: Check every relevant form control for its actual accessible name, including wrapping labels and ARIA; exempt hidden/decorative controls appropriately.

title: Notification delivery ignores each integration's selected events
trigger: Enable one success-only integration and a second failure-only integration, then run a passing suite.
impact: script.js only tests whether any integration wants the event, then sendNotification rereads all enabled integrations and broadcasts to every one. A failure-only destination receives successes and vice versa.
evidence: repro.cjs B15: PASSED goes to fail-only and success-only; disabled control is excluded. Actual call-site gate checked at script.js2692-2703 and2844-2855.
fix: Filter by each integration's notifyOnAll/notifyOnSuccess/notifyOnFailure in the delivery manager, rather than using a single global shouldNotify gate.

title: Duplicate DOM IDs route collaboration actions to unrelated controls
trigger: In Collaboration choose a JSON file or select a suite in Versions.
impact: import-file-input is duplicated at113/2646 and versions-list at1147/2748. getElementById resolves the earlier element: the collaboration picker uses the global import handler, while version history is rendered into a hidden standalone modal instead of the visible collaboration tab.
evidence: repro.cjs B16 verifies both duplicate pairs and collaboration history lookup; collaboration-ui2.js384 and index.html2649 target the duplicated IDs. Static DOM first-match contract establishes misrouting; no browser session required.
fix: Give collaboration controls unique IDs and update their labels, buttons, lookups and renderers; keep standalone version controls distinct.

title: Debugger Resume executes one step then pauses again
trigger: Start a two-step debug run and click Resume/F5 to continue.
impact: Resume and Step both merely resolve the current pause; the loop unconditionally pauses after each step regardless of chosen action. Continuous resume is unavailable and even the final completed step needs another Resume before the session finishes.
evidence: repro.cjs B18 runs the real debugger and creator loop with two stub DOM clicks: after Resume exactly one click occurs and isPaused=true; a third Resume is needed after two steps. debugger.js274-289 confirms identical resume primitive.
fix: Track run/step/pause mode explicitly; pause only on breakpoints, user pause or one-step completion, and do not pause beyond the last step.

title: Zero screenshot tolerance silently allows five percent difference
trigger: Set Compare Screenshot Diff Threshold % to0 for exact matching.
impact: parseFloat(...)/100||0.05 replaces intentional zero with5%; visual changes up to that percentage can pass despite the configured zero tolerance.
evidence: repro.cjs B19: threshold0 passes0.05 to assertions, while positive1 passes0.01.
fix: Default only when missing/NaN and validate the allowed percentage range while preserving zero.

title: Element picker emits invalid selectors for literal punctuation in IDs
trigger: Pick an element whose valid HTML id contains punctuation, for example id=form.email.
impact: The first and best-labelled suggestion becomes #form.email, which selects id=form with class=email instead of id=form.email. Colons and leading digits can also fail or select unintended elements; class and attribute suggestions have analogous escaping gaps.
evidence: repro.cjs B20 confirms the actual suggestion for literal id=form.email is #form.email. Static CSS selector semantics establish mismatch; query execution in a full browser was not run. Structural fallback also concatenates raw IDs at303.
fix: Use CSS.escape for identifier components and correct CSS-string escaping for quoted attribute values; validate suggested selectors against the selected element.

title: Saved input files are discarded by all language execution adapters
trigger: Save a Python, Java or C# suite with External Test Inputs and run it.
impact: The editor persists input_files, but execution reads inputFiles. Python receives no mock files and JDoodle receives empty stdin, so configured input is absent.
evidence: EXE-05 calls original executeSuiteCore with persisted input_files and observes an empty array at executePythonCode; a control using inputFiles delivers the same file. saveSuite writes input_files at line 2058.
fix: Use input_files consistently, including data-driven and imported suites, with migration only where needed.

title: Each data-driven execution appends a duplicate suite instead of updating it
trigger: Run a saved suite with a nonempty dataset using the default LocalStorage backend.
impact: Completion calls saveSuite(existingSuite), which always pushes an item. Identical IDs accumulate on every run, leaving duplicate cards and stale first-match metadata; remote add-only backends also create new records.
evidence: EXE-08 runs original runDataDrivenTest against original LocalStorageBackend: one stored ID becomes two copies of the same ID after one run. Original normal runTestSuite control updates and retains one record.
fix: Persist run metadata with updateSuite(suite.id, updates) for an existing suite; keep create and update operations distinct.

title: Expected Output is stored but never checked when running tests
trigger: Set a suite's Expected Output to a value different from successful program stdout and run it.
impact: The configured assertion has no effect. Any successful program with nonsuspicious output passes even when its output is completely wrong.
evidence: EXE-10 runs original runTestSuite with expected_output='must match': both matching output and 'completely different' return SUCCESS. Source reference assertion confirms suite.expected_output is used only to populate the editor; execution never compares it.
fix: Define the Expected Output comparison semantics and apply them in the shared execution path for both ordinary and data-driven runs.

title: The Unit Test node's individual Run button calls a nonexistent suite
trigger: Configure a Unit Test injection node and click its visible individual Run button.
impact: runNode handles Git, security-scan and AI nodes but not unit-test-runner. It calls runTestSuite(undefined), producing Suite not found instead of writing or running the configured test.
evidence: EXE-11 invokes original runNode: ordinary job passes its suite ID, while unit-test-runner passes undefined. The unit node has showRunBtn=true in render and its configuration has no suiteId.
fix: Route individual unit-test-runner execution through the same injection/command adapter as graph execution, or hide/disable the unsupported button.

title: Editing a saved graph mutates its live pipeline before Save
trigger: Open an existing graph, move/add nodes or edit node configuration, then close without saving and run/export the pipeline during the session.
impact: loadGraph stores the saved pipeline arrays and nested objects by reference. Unsaved edits alter the pipeline in memory and can later be persisted by another save/run; closing cannot discard changes.
evidence: EXE-12 calls original loadGraph then changes a node position and pushes a node; both changes appear in the original saved object immediately. Control loading a deep copy leaves the original unchanged. pipeline-manager.js line 565 passes the actual pipeline arrays.
fix: Deep-copy graph data into editor working state and copy back only on an explicit save/run action.

title: Security scan checkbox selections are ignored by pipeline execution
trigger: Configure a code Security Scan node to disable SAST/secrets and enable XSS, then execute a recognized security_scan node (for example imported schema or after EXE-02 is fixed).
impact: Editor saves booleans sast/secrets/xss, but runner reads scanConfig.scanTypes and falls back to ['sast','secrets']. Requested scan categories are not run and unchecked categories still run.
evidence: EXE-13 executes original graph callback with the editor's stored boolean schema and spies on scanner options: it receives sast/secrets. Explicit scanTypes:['xss'] control is respected. Source assertion confirms editor writes checkbox booleans at visual-editor.js lines 916-918.
fix: Convert stored checkbox choices to the scanner scanTypes array, or persist the canonical array from the editor; handle no categories explicitly.

title: Concurrent Playwright runs share and delete the same temporary script
trigger: Two Playwright IPC requests create their script file within the same millisecond, possible through repeated/bulk/concurrent invocation.
impact: Both use pw_test_<Date.now()>.js. The second overwrites the first script; the first callback can delete it before the other process opens it. Runs execute the wrong script or fail nondeterministically.
evidence: EXE-14 evaluates original runner using frozen Date and in-memory fs/exec: two pending runs have identical command paths and only the second script remains, then the first cleanup removes the shared file. Different timestamp control produces two independent files. No subprocess is started.
fix: Create unique temporary directories/files with mkdtemp or a cryptographic random identifier and clean up only the invocation's own file.

title: Editing a URL website suite throws before the editor opens
trigger: Click Edit on a website suite with website_method='url', or toggle the website method radios in index.html.
impact: Code and HTML call toggleWebsiteMethod, but the only implementation is named toggleWebsiteMethodInputs. ReferenceError interrupts openNormalSuiteEditor and method toggles fail.
evidence: EXE-15 calls original openNormalSuiteEditor on a URL website suite and asserts ReferenceError. Defining the missing alias to the existing method makes the same call complete. Neither source nor other tracked modules define toggleWebsiteMethod.
fix: Use the existing toggleWebsiteMethodInputs name in all callers, or export one intentional alias consistently.

title: A graph engine error leaves the previously saved SUCCESS status intact
trigger: Run a previously successful graph after connecting nodes into a cycle; the editor permits such connections.
impact: The catch path updates only the modal to ERROR and never persists lastStatus/lastRun. Stored/exported metadata still reports the old SUCCESS despite the latest run aborting.
evidence: EXE-16 runs original graph executor on a cyclic graph with lastStatus SUCCESS: UI says ERROR, lastStatus remains SUCCESS and savePipelines is never called. Acyclic success control updates lastRun and calls persistence.
fix: Persist an ERROR/FAILURE result and last-run timestamp in the exception path, preferably through a shared completion/finally routine.

title: Version writes resolve before the IndexedDB transaction commits
trigger: An IndexedDB put request succeeds and its containing readwrite transaction subsequently aborts or fails to commit, especially during migration.
impact: saveVersionHistory has already resolved. Migration then removes the original localStorage history at lines 141-144 without a committed replacement. DeleteVersionHistory has the same request-success handling at lines 91-96.
evidence: Static transaction-lifecycle proof: promises resolve on request.onsuccess with no transaction.oncomplete/onabort/onerror handlers. repro.cjs S03 models separate request and transaction events and confirms resolution while no completion event has fired. A real browser transaction abort or disk-failure experiment was not performed; the fixture proves the premature resolution, not an observed disk loss.
fix: Resolve writes/deletes on transaction.oncomplete, reject on transaction.onabort/onerror, and remove migration originals only after committed storage and verification.

title: Export All Suites produces a file the collaboration importer rejects
trigger: Use Export All Suites and then choose its downloaded JSON in the collaboration Import form.
impact: A valid application-generated bulk backup cannot be restored by the advertised collaboration import flow; it fails with missing suite data. Single-suite exports work.
evidence: repro.cjs S05 captures the generated blob: format=lvx-machina-bulk-export and suites=[...]. collaboration.js:338-345 requires suite and permits only lvx-machina-export, so the only reader used by handleImportFile rejects the exact exported output. The positive control round-trips a single-suite export.
fix: Recognize and validate both single and bulk formats and persist every imported suite with new local identities. Add a round-trip check between each export format and its public import path.

title: Email recipient modal serializes away the exported file Blob
trigger: Export a suite through Email Test Suite and click Send Email in its recipient modal.
impact: The inline handler receives blob:{} instead of the actual export Blob. The desktop fallback's URL.createObjectURL(exportResult.blob) at line 923 throws, so no valid attachment download or mail draft is produced. A Web Share File constructed from the object would contain the object string rather than suite JSON.
evidence: repro.cjs S06 creates the real exportForTeam Blob, renders the real modal, extracts its generated function argument and verifies JSON.stringify erased the Blob. Native Node URL.createObjectURL rejects that reconstructed object while the original is a Blob. No email client or external sharing action is invoked.
fix: Keep exportResult in a closure and attach a click listener to pass the real object, or store it under a transient ID and resolve the Blob on click. Do not JSON-serialize binary objects into handlers.

title: CSV parser splits valid multiline fields into multiple test rows
trigger:
Upload or manually enter a valid CSV whose quoted value contains a newline, such as name,note followed by Ada,"line1
line2".
impact: The parser resets quoting for every physical line, creating extra records and truncating/misaligning values. Data-driven tests run with incorrect row counts and content.
evidence: repro.cjs S07 verifies a normal quoted comma works, then the one-record multiline CSV becomes two data records and its note is only line1. The whole input is split before the quote-aware per-line parser runs.
fix: Use a CSV parser that maintains quote state across the entire input, or tokenize logical records before fields. Preserve content inside quoted fields and validate malformed records rather than silently truncating.

title: Opening and saving a dataset edit silently changes quoted field values
trigger: Create/import a row with a comma or quote in a field, click Edit and save it without changing any fields.
impact: The editor concatenates raw values into CSV. A stored x,y value is reinterpreted as two fields and extra fields are discarded by parseCSV, permanently changing it to x. Quotes can likewise disappear. Headers are also serialized raw here and by exportDataSet at line 331.
evidence: repro.cjs S08 creates a dataset with note=x,y, exercises actual editDataSet/saveManualDataSet and observes stored note=x. The initial save/read positive control retains x,y.
fix: Use one correct CSV serializer for header and value fields in both editing and export, quoting commas, quotes and line breaks. Pair it with the multiline-capable parser so unchanged edit/save and export/import round-trip exactly.

title: Variable substitution interprets literal data as regular expressions and replacement tokens
trigger: Use a CSV column name containing regular-expression punctuation, or a data/environment value containing replacement tokens such as $&.
impact: A dot in a header matches other names, an opening bracket can throw during test setup, and literal values such as $& are replaced with the matched variable text rather than the requested value. Environment replacement has the same replacement-string problem at environment-manager.js:88-91. Tests execute the wrong substituted input or fail before execution.
evidence: repro.cjs S09 has positive plain-value replacement, then verifies a.b matches aXb, a [ header throws, and $& leaves both dataset and environment placeholders unchanged. The ordinary caller is script.js:2625; environment caller is script.js:2506.
fix: Escape each key when building a regular expression and replace through a function that returns String(value), or use literal token replacement without regular expressions.

title: Security dashboard displays zero critical findings and perfect compliance for a failing scan
trigger: Open the Security reporting tab after recording a scan containing at least one critical vulnerability.
impact: Total vulnerabilities renders an object string, critical count is zero, severity chart is empty, and compliance is 100. The top-vulnerabilities table also says none because its expected per-vulnerability records are absent from stored scan history. These displays contradict the actual recorded failure.
evidence: repro.cjs S11 feeds a synthetic critical scan through the actual securityManager._saveToHistory/getStatistics and refreshSecurityDashboard. getStatistics returns severity counts in totalVulnerabilities (security-testing.js:875,884-887), while renderer expects bySeverity (reporting-dashboard.js:691,719,891). History stores only summary (security-testing.js:841-849), while renderTopVulnerabilities requires scan.vulnerabilities (reporting-dashboard.js:840-854). A direct correctly-shaped top-vulnerability input is the positive control.
fix: Define a shared statistics/history schema. Sum the severity-count object for the total, consistently use those counts for cards/charts/compliance, and persist the detail required by the table or explicitly state detail is unavailable.

title: Dashboard timeframe does not filter rankings and All Time truncates trends
trigger: Select a bounded timeframe with older executions outside it, or select All Time with executions older than 30 days.
impact: Summary and recent execution rows reflect the chosen timeframe, but slowest/most-run/flaky rankings use all stored history. All Time still sends 30 to the trend chart, omitting older runs that are counted in the summary. The same view presents contradictory execution populations.
evidence: repro.cjs S12 stores one recent pass and one 90-day-old failure. Seven-day total is one but slowest list contains Old; All Time total is two but line chart has only the recent day. Ranking methods independently read getHistory (lines 89-91,165-166,200-201).
fix: Pass the same filtered history to every dashboard widget, and represent an unbounded timeframe explicitly for trend generation instead of defaulting null to 30 days.

title: A failed replacement upload leaves the previous dataset available to save
trigger: Upload a valid CSV, select a second invalid CSV without closing the creation modal, then press Save.
impact: The error path does not clear currentUploadedData, hide the old preview or disable Save. Saving after the failed upload persists the previous file's rows under the current entered name, allowing an unintended dataset to be used in tests.
evidence: repro.cjs S15 opens the real creation flow, uploads a one-row First fixture, attempts an invalid one-line replacement, observes the parsing error and still-enabled Save, then saves and verifies First was persisted as Second upload.
fix: Invalidate currentUploadedData, preview and Save state immediately when a replacement upload starts and keep them invalid on errors. Guard asynchronous parse completion so an older file cannot replace a newer selection.

title: Datasets generated with the number pattern cannot be exported
trigger: Generate a dataset using {{number:5:5}} (or any nonzero number range), then click Export CSV.
impact: The generator stores numbers, but exportDataSet calls string.includes on their raw values. Export throws an uncaught TypeError before creating a file. Numeric zero is instead converted to an empty field by the || fallback, losing its value.
evidence: repro.cjs S16 exercises generateAndSaveDataSet with the real number pattern and confirms stored value 5, then exportDataSet throws includes is not a function. A dataset with the string value 5 exports successfully as the positive control. The number producer is data-manager.js:163-165.
fix: Convert non-null field values to strings before escaping and use a nullish/explicit missing-value check so zero is preserved. Share a typed-value-safe CSV serializer across export and editing.

title: Monaco warns on valid multiword Robot keywords
trigger: Edit a valid indented step such as Click Element    #submit.
impact: Validation splits on one space and checks only Click against full known keywords such as Click Element. Valid built-in commands are repeatedly marked Unknown keyword, undermining useful editor diagnostics.
evidence: repro.cjs B17: valid Click Element produces warning for Click; valid singleword Log control produces no such warning.
fix: Parse Robot cells using its actual separator syntax and compare the complete keyword cell; recognize assignments before keyword lookup.

title: Collaboration snapshot version numbers stop advancing after version 21
trigger: Create more than 21 collaboration snapshots for one suite.
impact: The retained history stays at 20 entries while the next version uses length+1. Versions 21, 22, 23 and later are all labelled Version 21, obscuring chronology and making version references ambiguous. Snapshot UUIDs remain distinct; this does not itself overwrite snapshots.
evidence: repro.cjs S14 creates 23 snapshots, confirms 20 retained entries and three separately retained snapshots all numbered 21.
fix: Calculate the next ordinal from the previous snapshot's version or keep a persistent monotonic counter independent of retention length.
